report.summary: Analyzed chunk 3 of 4 of graph.py: contains canonical_node, _graph_nodes, fenced_reachability, and fenced_dominance (partial). Verified claims about BFS, over-reporting, and document exclusion.
risks: _graph_nodes | medium | Claims to exclude documents but imports code_modules; no evidence documents are actually excluded beyond the docstring. | Check if code_modules excludes documents or if idx has a document flag.

fenced_reachability | medium | Claims to over-report non-Python edges; no mechanism visible in chunk to include non-Python edges. | Verify if idx contains non-Python edges or if over-reporting is aspirational.
fenced_dominance | low | Only partial docstring present; fraction calculation not implemented in chunk. | Complete implementation in next chunk.

handoff.purpose: Contains canonical_node, _graph_nodes, fenced_reachability, and start of fenced_dominance.

symbols.name: canonical_node
symbols.note: Returns canonical spelling of a node from the graph; uses _graph_nodes and case-insensitive fallback.

symbols.name: _graph_nodes
symbols.note: Returns set of all nodes in the dependency graph, excluding documents per docstring. Imports code_modules and uses import_edges and import_edges_reverse.

symbols.name: fenced_reachability
symbols.note: BFS from rel to find shortest dependency chain to a fenced module. Returns dict with reaches, hops, via, fenced_node, fragment, chain, visited, truncated, known.

symbols.name: fenced_dominance
symbols.note: Partial implementation; docstring only. Should compute fraction of non-fenced modules that feed a fenced module.

claims.text: documents are excluded deliberately, and this is a safety decision rather than a tidiness one
claims.why: No code in chunk filters out documents; relies on code_modules which is not shown.

claims.text: turning documents on would DILUTE the fence's dominance fraction with files that cannot reach anything
claims.why: Dominance fraction calculation not implemented in this chunk; claim about dilution cannot be verified.

claims.text: BFS over idx["import_edges_reverse"] (rel -> rels that import it), i.e. outward through everything that would be affected by editing rel
claims.why: Code uses rev = idx.get("import_edges_reverse") and traverses neighbours from rev.

claims.text: hops 0 means the edited path is itself fenced
claims.why: At start, hops=0; if frontier contains fenced node, returns with hops=0.

claims.text: hops >= 1 is the case the literal check cannot see: a leaf that a fenced module transitively depends on
claims.why: After each BFS level, hops increments; return includes hops value.

claims.text: Determinism is load-bearing: the frontier and every neighbour list are iterated sorted, first parent wins, and among fenced nodes found at the minimal hop level the lexicographically smallest is reported
claims.why: Frontier sorted before fenced check; neighbours sorted; first hit in sorted list is taken; chain reversed to show path.

claims.text: Non-Python import edges are best-effort, so this OVER-reports
claims.why: No mechanism to include non-Python edges visible in code; over-reporting cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: a spurious escalation costs a Claude call, a missed one lets a 7B model write code a hardware interlock depends on. Do not "tighten" this.
claims.why: Operational claim about consequences; no code to verify.

claims.text: An unknown path is still walked as given so a fenced-looking path is never let through merely for being absent from the graph.
claims.why: After canonical_node, if node is None, rel is used as-is: 'rel = node or rel'.

observations.what: _graph_nodes claims to exclude documents but the code does not show any exclusion logic; it imports code_modules and adds nodes from import_edges and import_edges_reverse. The exclusion must happen inside code_modules.
fenced_reachability uses a visit_cap default REACH_VISIT_CAP which is not defined in this chunk; likely imported or defined earlier.
fenced_fragment is used but not defined in this chunk; it must be defined elsewhere.
fenced_dominance docstring is present but implementation is missing; chunk ends after docstring.
